predecessors.name: Kingdom of the Franks
predecessors.text: Clotaire II's realm, from which Dagobert I granted 'a subkingdom in southern Aquitaine to his younger brother' Charibert II

successors.name: West Francia
successors.text: Cliopatria's West Franks shape from 896, which covers the duchy's land

successors.name: Duchy of Aquitaine
successors.text: the same duchy as Cliopatria resumes it in 990

ledger.x: 629: Dagobert I grants his half-brother Charibert II a subkingdom of Aquitaine with its capital at Toulouse.
632: Charibert II dies (8 April); 'Aquitaine passed again to Dagobert' and 'soon after that his infant son Chilperic was killed'.
731: Charles Martel crosses the Loire and takes Bourges.

732: Odo, beaten by the Umayyads near Bordeaux, asks Charles Martel for help and gets it 'in exchange for accepting formal Frankish overlordship'; Charles and Odo's allies beat the Umayyads at Tours in 732 and 'expelled them from Aquitaine'.
736: the last dated attack of Charles Martel on Hunald ('In 735 and 736 Martel attacked...').
760: Pepin the Short opens the War of Aquitaine.
781: Charlemagne makes his three-year-old son Louis king of Aquitaine.
845: the treaty of Charles the Bald and Pepin II.
ledger.cp: Rainulf I, count of Poitiers (new Duchy of Aquitaine)

ledger.x: 888: the duchy of the Poitevin counts is drawn as a state again.
893: 'Count Rainulf II was poisoned by order of King Charles III, or Charles the Simple.
895: Cliopatria's Aquitaine row ends, not the duchy.

wars.name: Battle of Toulouse (721)
wars.outcome: Odo 'inflicted a major defeat upon Al-Samh ibn Malik al-Khawlani at the Battle of Toulouse' on 9 June 721; no land changed.

wars.name: Umayyad raid of 732 and Battle of Tours
wars.outcome: The Umayyads under Abd al-Rahman 'raided Vasconia, advanced towards Bordeaux and ransacked the city' and beat Odo near Bordeaux; Odo accepted Frankish overlordship for help and the alliance beat them at Tours, expelling them from Aquitaine.

wars.name: Charles Martel's campaigns in Aquitaine
wars.outcome: Charles crossed the Loire in 731, 'ransacked Aquitaine twice, seizing Bourges', then in 735 and 736 attacked Hunald and the counts of Bourges and Limoges; Odo had accepted overlordship in 732.

wars.name: War of Aquitaine (Pepin the Short)
wars.outcome: After Pepin occupied Septimania (759) he fought 'a cyclical military campaign that lasted for eight years'; Waifer was assassinated in 768 and 'the autonomous and troublesome duchy of Aquitaine was conquered by the Franks in 769'.

certainty.note: No treaty line in the period fixes a frontier of Aquitaine; the Loire frontier, the Pyrenees and the Septimanian edge are approximate.
